The college is now run by a vice-commandant who interrogates and tortures cadets to find exactly those secrets, so Violet spends the year lying to her friends, avoiding Dain's memory-reading touch, and running errands for a revolution she is not always told the truth about, including the theft of what Aretia needs to raise its own protective wards. Xaden, posted away and bound to her by their dragons' mating bond, keeps hiding things from her for her own good, and the arguments between them are as central as the war. Alliance with Poromiel's gryphon fliers becomes real, bringing Cat Cordella and others to Basgiath. Violet is captured and tortured, and the confrontation everyone has been avoiding arrives at the college itself: the wards fail, venin and wyvern attack, her mother dies defending the school, and Xaden saves Violet by channelling dark power and becomes venin himself.

recaps.text: Previously: Violet Sorrengail was raised to be a scribe at Basgiath War College and ordered into the Riders Quadrant instead by her mother, the general who commands it. Physically fragile and marked out as the easiest kill in her year, she survived by preparation rather than strength, and at the Threshing she bonded two dragons at once, the powerful black morningstartail Tairn and the golden feathertail hatchling Andarna. Her signet turned out to be lightning, a power no living rider shares. Because Tairn is mated to Sgaeyl, she was forced into constant proximity with Xaden Riorson, the wingleader whose father led Tyrrendor's separatist rebellion and was executed by Violet's mother, and their hostility became an alliance and then a relationship. Sent on what was presented as routine border duty, her squad instead found the town of Resson under attack by wyvern and venin, dark wielders who drain the life from the land and who Navarre insists have been extinct for centuries. Her friend Liam Mairi was killed. Violet learned that the wards protecting Navarre are contracting, that villages have been abandoned in secret, and that Xaden and the marked riders have spent years arming Poromiel against the real enemy. Xaden took her to the rebel stronghold of Aretia, where her brother Brennan, mourned for six years, was alive.

Violet returns to Basgiath for her second year holding a set of secrets that would be treason if any of them were spoken aloud: the venin exist, the leadership knows, Aretia is rebuilding, and her brother is alive. The college has changed. A new vice-commandant, Major Varrish, has been installed with a mandate to root out disloyalty, and he is candid about his methods and openly interested in Violet, the marked riders and anyone who was at the border. Xaden has graduated and been posted away, so their dragons' mating bond, rather than any decision of theirs, dictates when they see each other. Among the first-years is Sloane Mairi, Liam's younger sister, who blames Violet for his death. Violet's own friends do not know what she knows, and every conversation is now a calculation about what she can safely say.

The year settles into two jobs done at once: being a second-year cadet, with all the sparring, flight duty and challenges that involves, and being a rebel inside a school hunting for rebels. Violet trains her lightning, which is still as dangerous to her as to anyone else, and works on being a rider whose body can be relied on. Dain's ability to read recent memories through touch turns an old friendship into a constant hazard. Varrish tightens surveillance, and cadets who attract his attention come back changed or not at all. Andarna, meanwhile, is changing in ways that worry Violet, and neither she nor Tairn will explain what is happening to her. Violet keeps digging in the archives, because the official history of the wards has holes in it that somebody deliberately cut.

The revolution's problem becomes concrete: Navarre's protection depends on a wardstone, and Aretia's was destroyed when the rebellion was crushed, so Tyrrendor is defenceless against the venin unless the rebels can raise a new one. That requires knowledge and equipment held at Basgiath, and Violet is the person inside. She works with Brennan, Xaden and the marked riders on a plan she is only partly briefed on, which becomes its own grievance, since Xaden's instinct is to protect her by keeping her ignorant and she has stopped accepting that. Keeping the plan and the people inside it hidden costs her the ordinary things: she lies to her own squad, she cannot be touched by an old friend without risking everyone, and the college's leadership is narrowing its search toward the people she is protecting.

The rebellion moves from arguing to acting. What Aretia needs is taken out of Basgiath and the work of raising Tyrrendor's own wards begins, along with the production of the alloy weapons that can actually kill a venin. The alliance with Poromiel stops being a smuggling arrangement and becomes official enough that gryphon fliers, including Cat Cordella, are brought into the college to train alongside riders, which almost nobody on either side welcomes. Violet is now openly balancing three loyalties, to her squad, to the revolution and to a relationship in which trust keeps having to be rebuilt. The secrecy she has been living under also fails where it always threatened to: Dain uses his signet on her and learns what she has been hiding, leaving her oldest friend holding the lives of everyone in Aretia. Andarna withdraws into a long sleep that no one will explain to her rider. At Basgiath, Varrish escalates, and the question is no longer whether the leadership will act against the rebels but how much of the school it will burn through to do it.

Varrish moves against Violet directly. She is taken, held and tortured for what she knows about Aretia and the revolution, and she is got out alive by the people around her rather than by anything the chain of command does. What follows strips away the last of the pretence on all sides. Xaden's secrets come out, including a second signet he has hidden for years because the law would have him killed for it, and Violet has to decide what she does with a truth he never volunteered. The venin's reach into Navarre proves to be closer and better placed than anyone at Basgiath admitted, including people the cadets thought were dead. With Aretia warded, Tyrrendor armed and the fliers allied, the confrontation that the kingdom's leadership spent a century avoiding is no longer avoidable, and it arrives at Basgiath itself.

Basgiath's wards fail and the venin attack with their wyvern. The battle for the college is enormously costly: much of the school is destroyed, riders and cadets die in numbers, and General Lilith Sorrengail is killed holding the line long enough for the defenders to organize, spending everything she has for a daughter she never learned how to speak to. Violet fights through the whole of it with her lightning, and Andarna emerges from her long sleep as something no one expected, changing what the defenders can do. The survivors end the book with the lie finally broken, a war that can no longer be denied, a real alliance with Poromiel, and Tyrrendor as the centre of the resistance. The last cost is Xaden's. To keep Violet alive he channels power from the earth the way the venin do, which works and which cannot be taken back. He hides what it has made him, and the book closes on the confirmation that the man leading the fight against the venin has become one.

characters.description: The Red-born hero of the revolution, now a decade older and worn down by a war that will not end. Once the hidden agent who toppled the old order, he is the most celebrated and feared soldier of the young Solar Republic, and its most divisive figure. Haunted by all he has done and losing patience with politics, he strains against the government he helped create, convinced that only relentless force can secure the freedom his people bled for.
characters.name: Darrow

characters.description: Darrow's wife and the leader of the Solar Republic, carrying the weight of a fragile new government at war. Brilliant, principled, and pragmatic, she tries to hold a fractious coalition together through law and compromise where Darrow would use the sword. Her marriage and her politics are both tested by the strain of an unfinished revolution.
characters.name: Virginia au Augustus

characters.description: Darrow's oldest and fiercest friend, still the savage heart of the Howlers, now older and a family man. Loyal to the last, he remains at Darrow's side through every danger, tempering his ferocity with a hard-won weariness. The years of war have marked him, but his devotion to Darrow has never wavered.
characters.name: Sevro au Barca

characters.description: A bold Gold warrior and wealthy heir who long ago threw in with the revolution and married Sevro. Fierce, blunt, and fiercely protective of her family, she remains a powerful ally to Darrow and Virginia and a formidable force in her own right.
characters.name: Victra au Barca

characters.description: The renowned swordsman and former enemy of Darrow who left the war behind to protect a child of the fallen ruling line. Living quietly in exile far from the Republic's reach, he has spent years as guardian and mentor to that boy, honoring a private code of honor while the worlds he once knew reshape themselves without him.
characters.name: Cassius au Bellona

characters.description: The grandson of the overthrown Sovereign, raised far from power by his guardian Cassius after the fall of the old regime. Now a thoughtful, idealistic young man, he has grown up on the fringes of a changed civilization, wrestling with the legacy of the family and order he was born into and with what he believes the worlds truly need.
characters.name: Lysander au Lune

characters.description: A young Red woman from a mining clan on Mars, displaced into a squalid resettlement camp after liberation failed to bring the better life she was promised. Sharp and dutiful, weighed down by responsibility for her family, she embodies the ordinary lowColors for whom the revolution's grand victories have not yet meant freedom or safety.
characters.name: Lyria

characters.description: A cynical Gray thief and criminal operator working the underworld of the new order, grieving a partner lost in the revolution. Bitter, clever, and out only for himself and his coin, he wants nothing to do with grand causes, though the schemes he takes on threaten to pull him back into events far larger than a simple job.
characters.name: Ephraim ti Horn

characters.description: The ruthless commander of the Gold forces still holding out against the Republic, infamous for scorched-earth cruelty during the war. Aging but implacable, he leads the remnant of the old regime and remains the Republic's great external enemy, determined to see the revolution crushed.
characters.name: The Ash Lord

recaps.text: Previously, in the first trilogy: Darrow was a Red, the lowest caste in a color-coded society, mining beneath Mars in the false belief his people were preparing the planet for humankind. After his wife Eo was executed for defiance, the rebel Sons of Ares revealed the truth and surgically remade him into a Gold, the ruling caste, then sent him to infiltrate the Institute, a brutal academy. Passing as a Gold, Darrow rose to prominence, gathered loyal allies such as Sevro, Victra, and the brilliant Virginia au Augustus, and spent years as a hidden agent climbing toward power. His rebellion, the Rising, endured betrayal, imprisonment, and enormous loss, and united Reds, Obsidians, lowColors, and sympathetic Golds against the ruling elite. In the end they overthrew the Sovereign, Octavia au Lune, and destroyed the treacherous Jackal, and Virginia founded a new government, the Solar Republic, meant to end caste tyranny and give every Color a voice. Darrow and Virginia married and had a son. But the war never fully ended: a remnant of Gold power fought on, and this book opens roughly a decade later, with the Republic strained, its promises unfulfilled for many, and its heroes divided over how to win a lasting peace.

characters.description: A scarred, undersized student whose long history of corrective surgery has not dulled his skill or ambition. Rei plans to take the CAD assignment exam and hopes to attend Galen's Institute with his closest friend, Viviana Arada.
characters.name: Rei

characters.description: Rei's only close friend at Grand Crest, a leading school combat scorer who openly defends him from hostile teammates. She shares his goal of receiving a CAD and entering Galen's Institute.
characters.name: Viviana Arada

characters.description: A hostile member of Rei's school combat team who treats Rei's physical limitations as a liability and publicly blames him after a tournament loss.
characters.name: Lee Jackson

characters.description: A highly trained prospective CAD user from the influential Laurent family. Pressured into a private evaluation by her controlling mother, she pursues Galen's summer program as an early route away from the family estate.
characters.name: Aria Laurent

characters.description: A controlling authority within Aria Laurent's family who values its reputation and expects Aria to excel. She directs Aria away from the public CAD exam and into a private evaluation.
characters.name: Aria Laurent's mother

characters.description: The sympathetic evaluator assigned to Rei's physical assessment. He recognizes Rei's determination but rejects him because the medical and performance results do not meet the required standard.
characters.name: Rei's physical examiner

characters.description: The artificial intelligence that governs the Inter-System Collective and conducts Rei's confidential final CAD interview through an avatar. It treats his unusual condition as a potentially valuable experimental variable.
characters.name: The Mind

characters.description: A celebrated former SCT competitor who later chose service at the front. At this point she is introduced only as an example of a fighter whose career extended beyond the tournament circuit.
characters.name: Valera Dent

characters.description: Rei's newly assigned A-type CAD. It begins at F8 with a single striking gauntlet and extremely weak specifications, but its unprecedented S-ranked Growth offers a path far beyond its initial state.
characters.name: Shido

characters.description: A D7 Mauler applicant whom Galen's Institute expects to compete for leadership among the incoming first years.
characters.name: Logan Grant

characters.description: Galen's SCT coordinator and principal arbiter. He opposes Rei's admission, arguing that Rei's low starting rank and medical history make him unsuitable for the Institute.
characters.name: Dyrk Reese

characters.description: The chief medical officer at Galen's Institute. After reviewing Rei's case, he believes Shido's genetic corrections may halt the illness behind Rei's many surgeries.
characters.name: Willem Mayd

characters.description: Aria Laurent's uncle, the commanding officer of Galen's Institute, and an experienced sparring partner. He practices phalanx footwork and defensive positioning with Aria and warns that unexpected contenders can displace favored Sectionals candidates.
characters.name: Aria Laurent's uncle

characters.description: A welcoming D5 Saber user assigned to Canes 304 with Rei and Viviana Arada. After meeting Rei, he checks the public record and immediately recognizes that his new roommate's history is unusual.
characters.name: Catcher

characters.description: A trusted assistant to Galen's commanding officer and a familiar figure to Aria Laurent. She gives Aria guarded guidance for interpreting the available evidence about Rei without disclosing confidential information.
characters.name: Galen's commanding officer's chief assistant

characters.description: A brawler instructor introduced among the staff of Galen's Institute.
characters.name: Michael Bretz

characters.description: A Lancer assigned to Canes 304 with Rei, Viviana Arada, and Catcher. Her initial introduction is simply as one of their new suite mates.
characters.name: Chancery Cash

characters.description: A D8 Brawler from the Galen's summer training program and the remaining member of the Canes 304 suite.
characters.name: Jack Benally

characters.description: A high-performing Brawler in Rei's class. He apologizes for his roommate's earlier confrontation with Rei, accepts that Rei cannot explain his unusual admission, and begins treating him with friendly respect.
characters.name: Bandt Senson

characters.description: A Saber classmate who defeats Rei in sanctioned training through superior rank, speed, and reach. He regards Rei's willingness to challenge stronger opponents as foolish.
characters.name: Mateus Selick

characters.description: A medical officer overseeing Rei's continuing treatment. She confirms that a suspected abnormal growth in his ankle has already resolved.
characters.name: Amina Ashton

characters.description: The highest-ranked Saber in Rei's class. She uses Magnetic Hunt to create an opening and defeats him in his first intraschool tournament match.
characters.name: Class 1A's top Saber

characters.description: An upper-year cadet who accepts Valera Dent's offer of personal training twice a week and agrees to use the second weekly session to help another cadet.
characters.name: Unnamed upper-year trainer

characters.description: A Brawler who previously trained alongside Rei and took part in the attack on him. She is named when the intraschool bracket assigns her as his next opponent.
characters.name: Camilla Warren

characters.description: The elite A-type mentor earlier assigned to Rei's group, also known on the field as the Lasher. His demanding instruction exposes each first year's habits and gives Rei experience against a far more advanced opponent.
characters.name: Christopher Lennon

characters.description: A Saber sub-instructor at Galen's Institute and former SCT competitor. Her exceptional defense supports a dangerous close-range style.
characters.name: Claire De Soto

characters.description: A Central Command authority whose directive forces the Galen's commander to alter the intraschool tournament despite strong objections.
characters.name: General Abel

characters.description: Catcher's full name, announced when he and Rei are reassigned to face each other in the sixth tournament round. He insists that they compete seriously, and Rei's victory eliminates him.
characters.name: Layton Catchwick

characters.description: A Central Command Sergeant Major who notices the high-priority alert generated by Rei's C4 development and immediately orders that General Abel be awakened.
characters.name: Cassidy Moran

characters.description: A powerful corporate authority who recognizes Rei in released tournament footage and urgently summons members of the family. The reason for that interest is not yet known.
characters.name: Head of Kamiya Corporation

characters.description: The public nickname newly attached to Rei after recordings of his intraschool matches circulate. Viewers connect the title with Valera Dent's own competitive identity.
characters.name: Iron Prince

recaps.ending: Rei defeats Logan Grant in the final individual qualifier by unveiling Shido's user-unique Type Shift. The ability converts Shido from its Brawler configuration into Saber mode, and the victory sends Rei to Sectionals. Aria Laurent becomes a squad leader and recruits Rei, Viviana Arada, Catcher, and Chancery Cash. The group still needs a Mauler, and Rei urges Aria to choose Logan despite their rivalry. Rei and Aria also agree to their first date. Released match footage gives Rei the public nickname Iron Prince and draws the unexplained attention of the head of Kamiya Corporation. Central Command is already monitoring and testing Rei, while Shido's future forms and limits remain unknown. Logan's family connection to Rei, Aria's conflict with her controlling family, Dyrk Reese's continued position at Galen's Institute, and the corporation's intentions all remain open.
recaps.in_short: Rei, a scarred student with a disabling bone disease, receives Shido, an initially weak A-type CAD with unprecedented S-ranked Growth. Valera Dent secures his admission to Galen's Institute, where Shido repairs his health and advances rapidly through every hard fight. Rei builds a trusted training circle with Viviana Arada, Catcher, and Aria Laurent while enduring hostility from Logan Grant, Mateus Selick, and Dyrk Reese. An ambush and a manipulated tournament bracket intensify the conflict, but Rei continues climbing through the intraschool competition. Central Command forces him to eliminate Catcher as a test, then pairs him with Logan. Intensive training brings Shido to C4 and unlocks Type Shift, a user-unique ability that changes it into Saber mode. Rei defeats Logan and qualifies for Sectionals. Aria forms a squad around their group, accepts a date with Rei, and considers Logan for its last position. Public footage earns Rei the name Iron Prince and alerts a powerful corporate family to his existence.

recaps.text:
Rei is a talented but physically disadvantaged student whose chronic condition has required repeated surgery. He and his closest friend, Viviana Arada, hope to receive CADs and attend Galen's Institute. Rei excels in the written assignment exam but fails the physical assessment. An unexplained system order overrides that rejection and sends him to a private final interview with the Mind, the artificial intelligence governing the Inter-System Collective. The Mind explains that Rei's unusual body makes him valuable as an experimental candidate, and Rei accepts the risk.

Viviana receives a strong Duelist CAD. Rei is selected last and receives Shido, an A-type CAD ranked only F8. Its first manifestation is a single gauntlet, and almost every specification begins near the bottom. One feature changes the meaning of that poor start: Shido has S-ranked Growth, an unprecedented rating. Viviana persuades Rei that this potential is worth pursuing. Despite the long odds of admission, they decide to apply to Galen's and spend the remaining months training.

Valera Dent brings Rei's application before the Galen's admissions board. She shows that he has already raised every ordinary specification and argues that his rapid development matters more than his starting rank. The board accepts him over Dyrk Reese's objections, while Willem Mayd predicts that Shido's genetic correction may end the illness behind Rei's surgeries. Dent later tests Rei's restraint during a confrontation at his old school before delivering his acceptance.

At Galen's, Rei and Viviana move into Canes 304 with Catcher, Chancery Cash, and Jack Benally. Rei also identifies Logan Grant, a highly ranked Mauler who immediately treats him with contempt. During commencement, Dent is revealed as Galen's chief combat instructor and former SCT star. Rei volunteers for a demonstration duel against Aria Laurent, the incoming class's only C-ranked cadet. He loses when Aria's Third Eye blocks his improvised blind-side attack, but he forces her to use the ability. The difficult fight raises Shido to E4 and produces its first physical evolution. Dent confirms that Shido's S-ranked Growth is driving the extraordinary response.

Rei's unusual admission and evolving CAD attract suspicion from other cadets. Aria investigates his public record and discovers that he rose from F8 at assignment to E4 within weeks. During parameter testing, Rei performs poorly in conventional agility and offense measures but shows rapid adaptation. In the fortitude assessment, his lifetime of extreme pain lets him endure to C2, far beyond his classmates, and earns new respect from Bandt Senson and the other Brawlers.

Live combat confirms that Rei remains badly outmatched in raw power. Viviana defeats him, and Logan then uses superior strength and a feint to win their bout. After the result is declared, Logan keeps attacking and tries to strike again. Dent intervenes, sends Logan to the brig, and warns Rei that cleverness alone will not always protect him. Shido converts the dangerous match into a major set of specification gains, reaches E7, and evolves again with greater speed and defense. Aria witnesses the immediate change and checks Rei's new rank, deepening her interest in the cause of his growth.

Rei begins extra evening training with Viviana and Catcher. Aria confronts him about his impossible rate of advancement, but instead of exposing him she asks for another fight and joins the group. Training against her helps Rei reach D0, while Aria gains the genuine friendships she has lacked under her family's control. The four become a close training circle, even as Aria's mother objects to Rei because of his background and rank.

Rei's visible improvement provokes greater hostility. Mateus Selick and five other first years lure him into a secluded sub-basement and attack him together. Rei manages to contact Aria before losing consciousness, and she carries him to the hospital. Catcher is allowed to inspect Shido and learns its S-ranked Growth. Rei refuses to name the attackers because there is no corroborating evidence and decides to answer them in sanctioned combat instead. Aria commits to preparing him for the coming intraschool SCT. Meanwhile, Viviana heads off to confront Logan, believing he arranged the ambush, while Catcher follows to stop the situation from worsening.

Viviana's confrontation reveals that Logan did not order the ambush. He gathers Selick and the other attackers, defeats them himself, and promises that they will not threaten Rei again, though his own hostility toward Rei continues. In class, Rei tells Logan that his conduct helped create the conditions for the attack. Aria publicly defends Rei, while Viviana remains unsettled by her private dealings with Logan.

Dyrk Reese openly calls Rei a burden during squad training. Rei answers defiantly and receives two days in the brig, leaving little preparation time before the intraschool tournament. Aria uses her family connection to Galen's commanding officer to train with him during confinement. Rei repays that trust by showing her Shido's S-ranked Growth. Back in parameter testing, Rei demonstrates major improvement, reaching C5 in offense and endurance and B0 in fortitude. Dent warns that his first tournament match may be difficult and observes that Shido has not yet developed a branch. The opening bracket confirms the danger: Aria must face Logan, while Rei expects an opponent considerably stronger than himself.

Aria defeats Logan after surviving his Overclock ability and advances in the winner's bracket. Rei loses his opening match to the strongest Saber in his class, despite injuring her and exposing her repeated patterns. The loss sends him into a demanding losers-bracket path, but Shido reaches D9 and evolves into a balanced two-armed configuration. Dent also arranges advanced instruction for Rei, Viviana, Catcher, and Aria with an elite A-type upper-year.

Rei's next pairing is Camilla Warren, one of the cadets involved in his ambush. By studying her habits, he defeats her with the tournament's fastest opening attack to that point. The lack of a Shido upgrade shows that preparation and skill, rather than superior specifications, decided the match. Galen's commanding officer then confronts Reese over a wider pattern of hostility toward Rei. Tournament records indicate manual interference from Reese's node, though the evidence is insufficient for formal punishment. Reese is ordered to restore automated randomization. School leadership also reveals that Central Command projects Rei may reach B or even A rank within his first year, while remaining concerned about the unknown risks of his growth.

Over the following tournament weeks, Rei wins three more matches while Aria, Viviana, and Chancery Cash qualify individually for Sectionals. Catcher remains in contention through the losers bracket. Christopher Lennon, the advanced A-type mentor known as the Lasher, pushes the group through punishing training and warns Rei that Shido may be approaching a major arsenal change.

An external order then overrides the expected bracket. Rei and Catcher are forced to face each other, and Catcher insists that they fight honestly. Rei wins, eliminating his friend and raising Shido to C3. Aria reveals that the order came from Central Command and that her uncle, Galen's commanding officer, opposed it. The group concludes that Central wanted to test whether Rei could defeat someone close to him. Rather than withdraw, Catcher immediately helps Rei prepare for the next match. With six days remaining, Rei commits to reaching C4, while Viviana supports the training and Aria secures a private field. Their trust survives the imposed contest, but Central's direct interest in Rei is now unmistakable.

Rei's next opponent is Logan. His attempt to force rapid advancement leaves him exhausted and predictable, so Christopher Lennon orders rest before taking control of the final preparation. Across a long Sunday session, Lennon targets Rei's balance, defense, endurance, cognition, speed, and ability to survive against a much stronger fighter. After repeated simulated defeats, Shido reaches C4 and evolves with an unknown, user-unique ability. Central Command receives an immediate alert, and Rei is placed under secrecy while Dent and Galen's medical staff evaluate the change.

In the final individual qualifier, Rei and Logan fight nearly evenly. Logan has greater mass and endurance, while Rei holds a slight speed advantage. After suffering severe wounds, Rei traps Logan's axe and activates Type Shift. Shido changes from its Brawler form into Saber mode, producing a sword and altered specifications. Logan activates Overclock, but Rei disables his arms and legs before the boost can turn the match. Rei wins by simulated fatal damage, qualifies for Sectionals, and establishes a limited new respect with Logan despite their continuing hostility.

Footage of Rei's victory reaches the head of Kamiya Corporation, who recognizes Rei rather than focusing on the match and urgently summons several family members. The reason for the corporation's interest is not disclosed.

At Galen's, Aria is selected to lead a Sectionals squad. She recruits Chancery Cash as the Lancer, adding her to a group that already includes Rei, Viviana Arada, and Catcher. Cash explains that she entered Galen's after failing her first CAD assignment examination, training for another year, and succeeding on a second attempt. The squad still lacks an aggressive Mauler. Rei proposes Logan Grant, judging him the strongest available choice despite their rivalry and Logan's failure to qualify individually. The invitation has not yet been made. Rei also asks Aria to spend a day alone with him during leave, and she accepts their first date. As public recordings circulate, viewers begin calling Rei the Iron Prince. He closes the term as a Sectionals qualifier with a user-unique CAD ability, a growing public identity, Central Command's attention, and an unexplained corporate family newly searching for him.
